name: Manorama Industries Ltd
tagline: High-ROCE specialty-fats / cocoa-butter-equivalent leader ('waste to wealth' from sal/mango/shea seeds) compounding ~40% with FY26 operating cash flow finally turning strongly positive - offset by a promoter-entity RPT and a re-rated ~45x multiple
business_overview: Manorama Industries makes specialty fats and butters - cocoa butter equivalents (CBE), cocoa butter alternatives, exotic-seed stearins - from tree-borne seeds (sal, mango, shea), supplying global chocolate and cosmetics majors. It runs a 'waste-to-wealth' model: procure exotic seeds in bulk (twice a year, India May-June and Africa November), fractionate without hydrogenation, and sell functional, price-stable alternatives to cocoa butter. It is backward-integrating in Africa (Burkina Faso 'Taang Kaam', new Chad subsidiary - eight African sourcing subsidiaries now) and building a Brazil presence.
fundamentals_table: FY24 +74%, FY25 +69%, FY26 +76% (Rs 1,358 Cr); Q1 FY27 +39.5% YoY (85% volume-led); EBITDA margin steady ~27%
FY26 CFO Rs 259 Cr (vs FY25 -Rs 59 Cr, FY24 -Rs 154 Cr); FY26 FCF Rs 206 Cr; debtor days 15 (from 48); inventory days ~349 (from 516)
Rs 500 Cr QIP done Jul-2026 at Rs 1,470 (ADIA-backed, ~2.8% dilution); net D/E 0.38 (from 0.83); Rs 460 Cr capex FY27-28 (FY27 spend Rs 225-250 Cr)
~45.3x trailing P/E (EPS Rs 44.25), ~16.2x P/B - re-rated back near its highs
fundamentals_narrative: The P&L remains outstanding: 35.4% ROCE, 40.3% ROE, FY24-26 revenue up 74/69/76%, and a Q1 FY27 that grew 39.5% (85% volume-led) with EBITDA +42% and PAT +67.6% (PAT margin flattered by ~Rs 13 Cr forex other income). The single biggest change this pass is cash conversion: FY26 operating cash flow turned strongly positive at Rs 259 Cr (versus -Rs 59 Cr in FY25 and -Rs 154 Cr in FY24) with FY26 FCF of Rs 206 Cr and debtor days down to 15 - the chronic negative-CFO bear thesis has, for now, inflected, though inventory days are still ~349. A Rs 500 Cr ADIA-backed QIP completed in July 2026 cut net D/E to 0.38 and pre-funds the Rs 460 Cr FY27-28 capex (Burkina Faso plant + India projects, major commissioning Q3 FY28). Against all this, the stock has re-rated back to ~45x earnings / ~16x book near its 52-week high, management withdrew explicit growth guidance, and the large recurring related-party purchases from promoter-owned Manorama Africa Ltd (RBI approval to consolidate pending since Aug-2023) remain unresolved.
technical_read: Not independently pulled. Stock has recovered to ~Rs 1,891, near the top of its Rs 1,060-2,043 band, reversing the earlier de-rating.

deep_dive.conviction_update: Medium-High -> Medium-High (firming within the band). The FY26 cash-flow inflection (CFO +Rs 259 Cr, FCF +Rs 206 Cr, debtor days 15) is a genuine, full-year, evidenced improvement on the core bear point, and the QIP de-risks the capex funding. But the ~45x re-rating, the withdrawal of explicit guidance, and the unresolved promoter-entity RPT keep it off High. Thesis-fit cut to 'neither' - a superb ~40% compounder, but at Rs 12,000 Cr and a full multiple a literal 10x in 2-3 years is not defensible.

sentiment_summary: Read the most recent 50 of 101 posts (Dec 2025 to Aug 2026). The dominant debate was whether falling cocoa/cocoa-butter prices threaten CBE demand and pricing - extensively argued and largely resolved by the community (Md_Uzair, GurpreetSingh, Girish_Kolari) that CBE is functionally decoupled from cocoa (used at ~5% of recipe, sticky approvals, shelf-life benefits, far less price-volatile) and that CBE is now only ~30% of revenue anyway, with value-added stearins the larger driver (CBE + stearins 71% of FY26 revenue). Trusted user Krishna_Kumar (elevated) is the cautious voice, arguing EBITDA margins could normalise toward 20-22% under customer pricing pressure - though margins have in fact held at ~27% through the cocoa-price fall. Trusted users Swadesh9819 and Aman_Jain3 (both elevated) are bullish. Secondary threads: negative cumulative CFO (now inflected positive in FY26), the Manorama Africa Ltd related-party purchases (~Rs 230 Cr in FY25, promoter-owned, pending RBI approval to become a subsidiary), and Nigeria's shea-nut export ban (management says minimal impact, ~6% dependency).
community_signal: Mixed-to-positive among trusted users. Swadesh9819 and Aman_Jain3 (elevated) are bullish on pricing power and the regulation-created demand; Krishna_Kumar (elevated) is the reasoned skeptic on margin sustainability - a thesis the FY26/Q1 FY27 margin prints (~27%) have not so far borne out. No trusted user has posted explicit 'core holding' sizing, but the lean is constructive, with the cocoa-linkage fear treated as largely debunked.
